meta.plant_name: Nakota Data Center Campus Power Plant

Equipment Manufacturer/Model.note: The binding letter of intent filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1462223/000168316826004843/nixxy_ex1001.htm says Baker Hughes committed NovaLT16 turbines of 16.9 megawatts each, in simple cycle. The model is spelled NovaLT16. The database spells it NovalT16 on units 1 and 2 and leaves unit 3 blank.

Backup Power.note: The announcement at https://hiranandaniltd.com/updates/hiranandani-backed-nidar-infrastructure-signs-binding-mou-and-offtake-agreement-with-tachyon9-nixxy-to-anchor-nakota-ai-data-campus-in-north-dakota/ describes dedicated behind-the-meter power generation fueled by natural gas for the data campus. That is the routine power supply for the campus, so Backup Power stays no.

Location Data Source.note: The letter of intent at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1462223/000168316826004843/nixxy_ex1001.htm places the campus on 620 acres about 5 miles west of Williston in Williams County. It gives no street address or parcel. This is offered as a live source for the dead Morningstar link. The point stays approximate.

Fuel Data Source.note: The press release at https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260609432974/en/ says the campus will run on natural gas from the Williston Basin. It is offered as a live source for the dead Morningstar link.

Status Data Source.note: The press release at https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260609432974/en/ says the first 150 megawatts are expected to be operational by the second quarter of 2027 and the campus is up to 1 gigawatt over a 36 month buildout. No air permit or commission case was found, so the status stays as in the database. It is offered as a live source for the dead Morningstar link.

Turbine/Engine Technology Data Source.note: The letter of intent at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1462223/000168316826004843/nixxy_ex1001.htm describes NovaLT16 gas turbines in simple cycle. It is offered as a live source for the dead Morningstar link.

qa.question: Is the Nakota campus about 5 miles west of Williston, or at the point now in the database?
qa.finding: The letter of intent at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1462223/000168316826004843/nixxy_ex1001.htm says the campus is about 5 miles west of Williston in Williams County. The database point is in open farmland about 28 kilometers northeast of Williston. Satellite imagery shows no site at either spot.
qa.recommendation: Keep the point as approximate. Ask the Williams County planning office or the developer for the parcel, and move all three units once it is known.
qa.note: A data tracking page at https://www.aterio.io/ shows a point near Epping in Williams County, which is a third guess and is not cited.

qa.question: Should each unit show 20 turbines of 16.9 megawatts, or 22 including spares?
qa.finding: The letter of intent at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1462223/000168316826004843/nixxy_ex1001.htm counts 22 NovaLT16 turbines per 300 megawatt phase, 20 operating and 2 spare, each 16.9 megawatts. The database uses 20 per unit, 338 megawatts, and 1,014 megawatts in all. The announced target is up to 1 gigawatt.
qa.recommendation: Keep 20 turbines and 338 megawatts per unit. The spares are not counted in capacity.
qa.note: The database technology is gas turbine, which matches the letter. The brief called the fleet engines, but these are turbines. No air permit exists yet to confirm the count.
